Reasonable aliases drawn from PSI title and common usage
psi-map.json maps acme-e-field to PSI-22; brief lists E-FIELD as one of six ACME experiments
PSI-22.investigationEndDate is 11-17-2020, confirming flown status
PSI-22 record exists in local PSI data

Matches PSI-22.objective verbatim and NASA Science page paraphrase

PSI researchImpacts states 'not being conducted to serve any space applications'; ACME doc says primary goal is terrestrial efficiency, secondary is fire prevention. Classification as 'fundamental' is correct; confidence 'medium' appropriate for interpretive step
PSI approach: 'experiment is conducted with gas-fueled flames'; brief: 'six ACME experiments featured flames of gaseous fuels'
PSI approach: 'Methane and ethylene were used as fuels'; PSI-22.csv fuel bottles: 100% CH4, 40% CH4, 100% C2H4, 30% C2H4

PSI approach describes gas-jet burner (no coflow) and coflow burner (weak synthetic air coflow) with flat circular copper mesh electrode; NASA ACME doc confirms both configurations and mesh at 35 or 50 mm
PSI-22.experimentHardware: 'Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), ACME'; brief: ACME hardware in CIR on ISS

NASA ACME doc: ACME chamber insert with exchangeable burner, hot-wire igniter, gas delivery, high-voltage supply, crew-removable electrode mesh settable +10/-10 kV at 35 or 50 mm; PSI approach confirms high-voltage copper mesh electrode up to 10 kV

Lists 4 of 5 other ACME experiments (acme-bre, acme-cld-flame, acme-s-flames, acme-cfi-g); missing acme-flame-design (PSI-10) which psi-map.json notes as 'sixth ACME experiment; no seed record yet'. Not incorrect but incomplete.
Correctly null: conditions.json shows null o2 for PSI-22; PSI-22.csv has no O2 column; no readable source states numeric O2 range
Correctly null: conditions.json shows null pressure for PSI-22; PSI-22.csv has no pressure column; NASA ACME doc says constant-volume with pressure rise but gives no values
Correctly null: PSI-22.csv has no airflow column; PSI approach and NASA ACME doc state coflow velocity was varied but no numeric values given in readable sources

PSI-22.projectType 'Microgravity Investigation'; brief states flew in microgravity and only mimics partial gravity electrically. Value min=0, max=0 correct. Confidence could be 'high' (direct PSI statement) rather than 'medium'.
PSI approach: 'Methane and ethylene were used as fuels and diluted with nitrogen to control flame strength'

PSI approach: 'Parameters such as fuel flow rate, coflow velocity, and field polarity were varied'; PSI-22.csv varies mesh polarity, fuel bottle, fuel concentration (25-100%), and burner type (coflow vs gas-jet rounds)

PSI approach: 'All experiments were conducted in the combustion integrated rack (CIR)'; NASA ACME doc: constant-volume studies, ~90 L chamber, 0.5-2 minute tests, same modular hardware. Note correctly states chamber atmosphere composition not stated.

PSI approach: high-res cameras, spectral imaging, thermopile detectors, ion current measurement; NASA ACME doc: ion current via voltage drop, PMT array, thin-filament pyrometry fibers, radiometers, CIR gas chromatograph for pre/post atmosphere

Accurately reflects brief: 'Partial gravity was mimicked in ACME's E-FIELD Flames experiment through the effect of the electric field on the ions that naturally occur in flames' and 'there is currently no partial-gravity combustion data available in PSI'

PSI researchImpacts: electric field control reduces pollutants, enables more efficient combustion, soot control; NASA ACME doc: primary goal is improve efficiency and reduce pollutant emission in terrestrial combustion

All three papers present in PSI-22.publications: (1) Chien et al. 2022 Combust Flame DOI 10.1016/j.combustflame.2022.112443, (2) Tinajero & Dunn-Rankin 2018 Combust Flame DOI 10.1016/j.combustflame.2018.10.036, (3) Chien et al. 'Ion Current and Flame Changes with Electric Fields in Microgravity' DOI 10.60555/se5a-8c73
